close_reason: Added debug_assert! to SetError::with_extra that panics on reserved wire-name keys, plus pub const RESERVED_SET_ERROR_WIRE_NAMES exposing the 8 typed-field wire names. Three tests: panic-on-each-reserved-name iterates the full constant; positive-control proves a non-reserved key still works; serialize-time invariant proves the constant covers every typed wire-name field on the SetError surface, so adding a typed field without extending the constant is caught at next test run. jmap-types::SetError has no with_extra builder (extras assigned to pub field directly) so this fix is scoped to jmap-server::backend::SetError only.
description:
Scenario: a future contributor (or you, in 12 months) writes SetError::new(SetErrorType::Forbidden).with_extra("type", json!("customType")) intending to override the wire 'type' field. Because SetError.extra uses #[serde(flatten)] (crate-jmap-server/src/backend.rs:69), and SetError.error_type also serializes as the "type" wire field (#[serde(rename = "type")] at backend.rs:23), the resulting JSON has two "type" keys at the same level. serde_json will emit both — which is technically malformed JSON per RFC 8259 §4 ('an implementation … may report differing values for the various names'). The serializer happily produces this output; the consumer's JMAP client may pick either value depending on its JSON parser.

The doc comment at with_extra (backend.rs:151-157) warns: 'Calling with_extra("type", ...), with_extra("properties", ...), or any other reserved wire-name will produce a malformed SetError on the wire — callers are responsible for choosing extension-namespace keys that do not collide with the typed-field wire names.'

The warning is correct but the API silently accepts the unsafe call. A debug_assert! at the with_extra body checking against the known reserved wire-names ("type", "description", "properties", "existingId", "maxRecipients", "invalidRecipients", "notFound", "maxSize") would catch the bug at the first test run. Production builds would not pay any cost (debug_assert! is no-op in release).

Maintenance consequence: a quietly-malformed wire response, surfaced only via a downstream client filing a bug ('SetError fields out of order' or 'why is description missing'). The reproducer is invisible to the server team because the server-side tests don't exercise reserved-name collisions and the API permits them at compile time. This bead also covers the parallel jmap-types SetError type referenced in the doc comment, if it has the same shape.
title: SetError.with_extra silently accepts reserved wire-name keys, producing malformed JSON
